novel_mechanics_found: HEADLINE: bp35 L6 has a HARD ACTION-COUNT TIMER. Three independent fresh-env runs all hit GAME_OVER at EXACTLY total action 228 from reset (i.e. 63 usable L6 actions after the fixed 164-action L5 prefix), reproduced in three different situations: (1) mid-undo-rewind at (7,31), (2) mid-click-sweep at (8,31), (3) standing still at high ground (6,21) doing pure ACTION5 no-op waits with zero state change. The death is position-independent and invisible (no riser object, no object-list change) -- it is a hard cap, and EVERY action (moves, clicks, no-ops, undos) consumes it. This retroactively explains the historical 'stepping RIGHT out of the notch is LETHAL' finding: those attempts spent ~60 actions exploring, then stepped -- the timer killed them, not the step. I stepped right out of the notch (5,30)->(6,30) TWICE, alive, early in the budget. Other mechanics: (a) round-7's strongest lead CONFIRMED: clicking switch 2 (world (4,31), display (27,29)) after only 2 lefts (player at (6,31)) lands the player alive at (6,30), and from there the whole upper region opens: RIGHT->(7,30), RIGHT->float up column 8 to a lip-perch at (8,23), LEFT->(7,23), LEFT->float up the consumed-switch-1 chimney (6,22) to (6,21), then a row-21 corridor spanning columns 2-7 (walled at (1,21), ceiling row 20 solid at cols 5-8 with clickable X-blocks at (2,20),(3,20),(4,20)); (b) ACTION7 undo is DEEP (26+ presses, not 6): per-press it reverses ONE action including full player-position restore, and can rewind across the gravity-flip (restoring switch 2 un-consumed + gravity down + pre-click position) -- but each undo costs a timer action, making deep rewind a timer trap; (c) ACTION1 and ACTION2 are NOT inert: both move the player LEFT (round 7 tested them only at (5,30) where left is walled); ACTION5 is a true no-op; (d) click mapping: display=(world_x*6+3-cam_x, world_y*6+3-cam_y), camera y follows player row (values 90/102/144/160 observed), off-screen (negative-y) clicks are no-ops, so the row-13 X-blocks and switch 3 at (8,1) are unclickable from every reachable cell (needs player row <=20; row 20 is fully sealed); (e) ~60-cell click-sweep of statics (left region, goal room walls rows 28-34 cols 1-4, sub-floor rows 33-34) found ZERO hidden E-tiles; goal diamond (2,31), hzusueifitk (2,15) and blocked cells never respond to clicks; (f) after GAME_OVER an in-place env.reset() does NOT restore bp35 cleanly (prefix replay desyncs and dies at level 0) -- always build a FRESH arcade env; that mistake cost 164 steps.
narrative: Precondition: resolved the 164-action banked plan via resolve_replay_plan and replayed it on a fresh offline env -- frame_level==5 at exactly 164 steps, player (3,23). RUN 1: executed round-7's strongest lead -- the known-safe route to the shaft (solidify X-shields at display (39,51)/(45,51) = world (6,25)/(7,25), 3 rights, switch 1 at (39,33)=(6,22) which drops the floor cell, 2 rights falling down column 8 to (8,31)) then only TWO lefts to (6,31) before clicking switch 2 at (27,29)=(4,31). Result: NEW alive landing at (6,30) (round 7's notch problem bypassed). From there mapped the pocket (5-7,30), discovered A1/A2 move left, floated up column 8 to a lip at (8,23), walked left and floated up the consumed-switch-1 chimney to (6,21), solidified the three row-20 X-blocks by click, and walked the row-21 corridor to its left wall at (2,21). Corridor is a dead end (row 20 sealed above; (1,21) walled; hzusueifitk (2,15) click-inert). Tested ACTION7: found deep per-action rewind with position restore; rewound 26 presses back across the switch-2 click (gravity down + switch restored at (6,31)) -- then died at total action 228, which at the time looked like an undo-boundary quirk. In-place reset then desynced (164 steps lost). RUN 2 (fresh env): probed the never-explored LEFT side of the L5 shelf -- (2,23) is a 1-cell alcove walled at column 1 with solid floor (null); A1/A2/A5 inert with gravity down; 17-click sweep of the left region statics (null); route to (8,31) and a 19-click sweep of the goal-room walls (null); extended sweep of sub-floor rows 33-34 -- died at run-action 228 mid-sweep, briefly misattributed to a 'floor door' at (7,33). RUN 3 (fresh env): re-clicked (45,41) from (6,31) -- inert, falsifying the door theory; climbed to (6,21) in 5 actions and sat on ACTION5 no-ops watching: GAME_OVER at exactly run-action 228 with zero object changes -- proving the position-independent hard action timer. Budget (950 env-steps) then forbade a fourth run. Net: no new level banked, but the level's true constraint (63-action post-prefix speedrun) and a corrected mechanics model are now known, plus one concrete untested exit: the (8,21) column-8 upper float (see gotchas).
gotchas: TIMER: bp35 dies at EXACTLY total action 228 from reset (63 L6 actions after the 164-action prefix). Plan every route as a speedrun; no-ops, clicks and undos all burn budget. If the timer is per-level rather than per-run, a shorter L1-L5 prefix would buy more L6 budget -- worth testing with a trimmed prefix.
The historical 'lethal right step out of the notch' is a MYTH: it was the timer. (5,30)->(6,30) is safe (with the (6,25)/(7,25) shields solidified). Do not fear the pocket; fear the clock.

Best-known-value route (18 post-prefix actions, timer-safe): 2 shield-clicks, 3xRIGHT, switch-1 click, 2xRIGHT (fall to (8,31)), 2xLEFT, click switch2 at (27,29) from (6,31) -> alive at (6,30); then RIGHT,RIGHT (float to (8,23)), LEFT,LEFT (chimney float to (6,21)) -> row-21 corridor; 3 clicks solidify (2..4,20); 4xLEFT -> (2,21). Arrives ~action 189 leaving ~38 actions.

THE ROUND-9 MOVE (untested, 50/50): from the corridor, step RIGHT from (7,21) to (8,21). Column 8 above the (8,22) lip is open at row 21; the float goes up toward the OPEN X-hazard at (8,13). If hazards are solid-blocking, you perch at (8,14) with camera ~55 making row 13 + hzusueifitk/ubhhgljbnpu region clickable/reachable -- the only path toward switch 3 at (8,1) and the sealed upper-left. If hazards are overlap-lethal, you die. All prior 'pillar extent' evidence is debunked (timer), so solidity is genuinely unknown. Timer-wise it fits easily (~action 190).

Do NOT deep-rewind with ACTION7 as a reset substitute: 26 undos = 26 timer actions; the rewind works perfectly (full position+state restore per action, crosses the gravity flip) but eats the budget that killed run 1.
After GAME_OVER, never env.reset() in place for bp35 -- the prefix desyncs and dies at level 0. Build a fresh Arcade env (costs nothing but RAM).

Click mapping: display=(wx*6+3-camx, wy*6+3-camy); camera-y tracks player row; negative/off-screen clicks are silently inert (round 7's (15,-51) and every row-13 target). Player row <=20 is required to click row 13, and row 20 is fully sealed -- only the (8,21) float can get above it.
A1/A2 both move LEFT (redundant with A3 as far as observed); A5 is a pure no-op; the entire L1-L5 prefix uses only 3/4/6, so 1/2/5/7 semantics were unknown until now.

Statics are inert to clicks everywhere swept (~60 cells: left region rows 17-24 cols 1-2, goal-room walls rows 28-34 cols 1-4, sub-floor rows 33-34 cols 1-8, pocket periphery). The goal room has NO clickable entrance; if it opens at all, it is via the upper region or a mechanism above row 20.

Object glossary (world coords at L6 start): goal fjlzdjxhant (2,31); gravity/consumable switches lrpkmzabbfa (4,31)=switch2, (6,22)=switch1 [drops the (6,24) floor], (8,1)=switch3 UNREACHED; X-blocks oonshderxef(open-hazard)/yuuqpmlxorv(solid): rows 13 (cols 2,3,4,5,7,8 open + 6 solid), 20 (cols 2,3,4), 25 (cols 6,7); touch-objects hzusueifitk (2,15) orange-outlined + ubhhgljbnpu (2,10), both click-inert and unreached.
